summary: Handshake ripple: connection reuse + session migration causing upstream throttling and runtime crash-loop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer OrbitChat reported an abrupt surge in 5xx responses for a subset of streaming and short-text generation requests. Errors correlate with a tenant traffic pattern that triggers many concurrent TLS session migrations and high prefetch activity.

Impact:
- ~18% elevation in 5xx rate for tenant OrbitChat over a 40-minute window (prod us-east).
- Streaming sessions experienced frequent resets; short requests hit intermittent 502/503.
- Customer-visible latency spikes and degraded throughput. No data loss reported.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted (dedicated GPU pool for OrbitChat).
- us-east region; API gateway (edge) -> regional LB -> runtime fleet behind prefetcher.
- Models: redwood-open-3b (primary), fallback redwood-opt-7b.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant connection churn increases when client rotates underlying IPs or resumes sessions (session migration).
2) Edge reuses connections aggressively (keepalive/conn-reuse path) while handshake state migrates, producing short bursts of half-open sockets forwarded to regional LB.
3) Prefetcher concurrently starts several model hot-loads and KV cache warmups for new sessions.
4) Runtimes accept queue becomes backlogged -> worker threads see fragmented GPU memory allocations -> some workers crash and restart -> upstream 5xx amplification due to retries.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway logs show many connection-level RSTs and short TLS renegotiation windows during the incident window.
- Region LB metrics show accept_queue_depth spike and SYN/ACK retransmits.
- Runtime logs show repeated "gpu_allocator_fragmentation" warnings followed by watchdog-triggered process exits.

Expected behavior:
- Connection reuse should not cause cascading accept queue pressure or trigger runtime GPU fragmentation under normal prefetch loads.

Relevant logs/metrics (links):
- Edge traces (sample): https://observability.redwood.ai/traces/edge/trace/0a1b2c
- LB accept queue dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/dashboards/accept-queue/us-east
- Runtime crash logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/runtime/2026-03-12/cluster-17

2026-03-12 10:02 - Jordan Lee (on-call SRE): Correlated edge and LB metrics; accept_queue_depth spike aligns with customer timestamps. Elevated SYN/ACK retransmits and short TLS renegotiation windows visible.

2026-03-12 11:45 - Maya Patel (Serving eng): Found repeated gpu_allocator_fragmentation warnings in runtimes followed by watchdog exits. Hypothesis: backlog increases memory fragmentation when prefetch inflight tasks allocate mixed-size buffers.
2026-03-13 08:20 - Jordan Lee: Mitigated customer impact with temporary workarounds (see investigation notes). Monitoring shows 5xx rate reduced to baseline for OrbitChat after edge change.

investigation_notes: Edge/Proxy: keepalive/conn-reuse code path reuses sockets aggressively when session migration occurs (client IP change). This produced a short-lived burst of half-open connections forwarded to region LB.
LB: accept_queue_depth for cluster-17 spiked from baseline ~5 to >250 during bursts; kernel-level socket backlog saw drops. LB did not reject but queued connections longer than SLO.

Runtime: prefetcher triggered multiple concurrent model preloads for new sessions; combined allocation patterns (large KV cache chunks + temporary attention caches) increased GPU fragmentation in a narrow time window.

Crash pattern: workers hit fragmentation threshold then OOM guard/tracker triggered watchdog restarts. Restarted workers rejoin but with warmup cost -> amplification of in-flight requests and retries -> more load on LB/edge.

Repro: Synthetic test reproducing session-migration pattern against staging with high prefetch concurrency reproduced accept queue spike and runtime allocator warnings. Lowering prefetch concurrency eliminated the crash pattern in tests.

Hypothesis: the root cause is an interaction between aggressive connection reuse at the edge, LB accept queue sizing/behavior under session-migration churn, and the runtime's allocator behavior under a burst of heterogeneous allocations from prefetching.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds applied (temporary):
- Edge config: disabled TCP connection reuse for OrbitChat tenant for the next 4 hours to avoid session-migration amplification.
- Prefetcher throttling: lowered concurrent prefetch parallelism for the tenant group via config flags.
- LB tweak: increased accept queue backlog size and tuned kernel tcp_max_syn_backlog on cluster hosts.
Result: 5xx rate for OrbitChat returned to baseline within 12 minutes of changes.

Permanent fixes planned (follow-up actions):
- Runtime: add a defensive allocator path to reduce fragmentation under mixed-size concurrent allocations (ENG-5543).
- Edge: add detection/guard when session-migration pattern detected to reduce conn-reuse on-the-fly (ENG-5581).
- LB: consider proactive connection shedding or early backpressure propagation to edge when accept queue exceeds threshold (INFRA-3497).
- Create a postmortem and update handshake/failure-mode runbook.

Rollout notes:
- Runtime allocator patch targeted for canary on cluster-17 first, then gradual rollout across fleets. Estimated PR and canary week: 2026-03-21.
- Edge guard to be feature-flagged and rolled in two phases; initial monitoring for false positives planned.

Customer communication:
- 2026-03-13 09:00: Proactively messaged OrbitChat with status and workaround steps; provided timeline for permanent fixes.
- Customer acknowledged workaround and requested postmortem after permanent fix rollout.
